current_scheme: No AI Diffusion tiers. BIS announced on 12-13 May 2025 it would not enforce the Jan 2025 AI Diffusion Rule; no replacement rule has issued, and on 14 Jul 2026 Under Secretary Kessler told Congress none is intended (new rulemaking instead). The CFR text of 15 CFR 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A) still reads as a worldwide licence requirement with per-country TPP allocations, but BIS enforces it only as the pre-Diffusion scheme: (1) destination-based licence requirement for 3A090/4A090 and related .z items to Country Groups D:1, D:4, D:5 and Macau, excluding destinations also in A:5 or A:6; review is presumption of denial for D:5 and Macau, presumption of approval for other D:1/D:4 destinations; (2) per BIS guidance of 31 May 2026, a worldwide licence requirement where the buyer is headquartered in, or its ultimate parent is headquartered in, D:5 or Macau (originally 744.23(a)(3), now 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A)). Modifications: FR 2026-00789 (eff. 15 Jan 2026) case-by-case review for US-origin exports to China/Macau of chips below TPP 21,000 and DRAM bandwidth 6,500 GB/s (H200-class), with conditions; FR 2026-14132 (eff. 10 Jul 2026) moved the UAE to A:5 while expressly retaining a UAE licence requirement with an approved-entity exemption (Supp. 8 to Part 740); FR 2026-02262 (eff. 3 Feb 2026) removed Cambodia from D:5. Part 744 end-use/end-user controls (Entity List, military/WMD, May 2025 AI-training policy statement) and GP10 guidance on Huawei Ascend apply everywhere. The American AI Exports Program (EO 14320, 23 Jul 2025) is promotional and has not been found to create a licence exemption.

notes: The CFR text of 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A)/(b)(10) still contains the AI Diffusion worldwide licence requirement, supplement 5 country lists and the 790M-TPP per-country allocation. Coding follows BIS's announced non-enforcement plus the May 31 2026 guidance, i.e. the pre-Diffusion D:1/D:4/D:5/Macau scheme. This is enforcement policy, not regulatory text: it could change without a Federal Register rule, and GAO (12 May 2026) found the non-enforcement announcement was itself a 'rule' under the CRA.

The D:1/D:4 'presumption of approval' and the A:5/A:6 exclusion come from a January 2024 secondary source (Fenwick) describing the Oct/Nov 2023 rule. The 2023 FR text and BIS FAQs were not fetched directly in this run. Verify before relying on the review-policy distinction between license_required and license_presumption_denial.

Israel (D:4, but A:6) is coded under the default (no destination licence) because of the A:5/A:6 exclusion. The same exclusion applies to any D-group member in A:5/A:6; only Israel currently qualifies.

UAE: the .a-item licence requirement for the UAE sits in 742.6(a)(6)(iii)(A), the paragraph that is otherwise unenforced outside D:5/Macau. Law-firm summaries say BIS expressly retained it for the UAE in FR 2026-14132, but the rule text and preamble were not fetched directly. The review policy for UAE parties not on Supp. 8 is not established. The individual US-company subsidiaries on Supp. 8 were not named in the sources fetched. The G42/Core42 listing expires 6 Apr 2027.

Saudi Arabia is still in D:4 (and D:3), so it is coded license_required. HUMAIN's Nov 2025 authorisation is a licensing decision, not a regulatory carve-out. No Saudi rule equivalent to the UAE's was found, but the absence of a Sept-Oct 2026 Saudi rule was not exhaustively confirmed. The Arnold & Porter commentary suggests the UAE rule is 'the template' for other Gulf partners.

China: the H200-class case-by-case policy (FR 2026-00789) covers only exports from the US. PRC authorities reportedly blocked or discouraged H200 imports from Jan 2026, and licences for small volumes were reported in Feb 2026. Whether licences have been granted or revoked since is not confirmed as of Oct 2026. The 25% duty and revenue arrangements are tariff/commercial measures, not EAR terms.

Russia and Belarus face additional EAR 746.8 restrictions (licence for all CCL items, policy of denial). These were not separately fetched this run. Coded license_presumption_denial on D:5 grounds, not 'embargoed'. A stricter reading would code them embargoed.

Syria: the comprehensive embargo was relaxed (Sept 2025) and the SST designation was rescinded, but Syria is still in E:1 and D:5 per the Aug 2026 Steptoe post and the current bis.gov country groups. It is coded license_presumption_denial, not embargoed. The status of advanced computing items to Syria was not addressed in the fetched source.

Malaysia and Thailand: a US rule imposing AI-chip licence requirements was reported as planned in July 2025, but no issued rule was found. Both are coded under the default. Malaysia's own domestic export permit for US AI chips is out of scope for this layer.

No issued replacement framework was found. A compute-threshold global licensing framework (GB300-equivalent tiers, host-government investment matching) was reported in draft in March 2026 and denied by Commerce. Kessler told Congress on 14 Jul 2026 that no AI Diffusion replacement is intended. Rules published 15 Sep to 20 Oct 2026 were checked only by search, so a very recent rule could be missed.
The American AI Exports Program (EO 14320, 23 Jul 2025) is promotional and is not coded as a licence exemption for any country. No country-level 'full-stack package' licence exemption was found.

Entity-level controls (Entity List, the D:5/Macau headquarters test, the Part 744 military/WMD/AI-training policy statement, GP10 for Huawei Ascend) apply in every country, including default ones. This layer codes destination posture only, so a 'no_license_required_general' country can still host restricted end users.

The country-group memberships come from bis.gov node/9171 and Cornell LII, both fetched 2026-10-20 and consistent with each other (UAE in A:5 and out of D:4; Cambodia out of D:5). Neither page shows its last-amended date.

Sources marked 'seen in search results, not fetched' (FR public-inspection PDF 2026-00789, Bloomberg Government on G42/HUMAIN, MoFo on Syria) are corroborating references only. Their content was not read.
